title: function default_version in py3versions.py fails if os.readlink('/usr/bin/python3') returns a link
description:
Instead of simple read the link

_default_version = os.readlink('/usr/bin/python3')

an use it I add the loop:

while os.path.islink(_default_version):
    _default_version = os.readlink(_default_version)

this will resolve the true target/of python
commit_message:
function default_version in py3versions.py fails if os.readlink('/usr/bin/python3') returns a link

When upgrading python3-twisted (ubuntu 18.04) I got the error:
ValueError: the symlink /usr/bin/python3 does not point to the python3 default version. It must be reset to point to python3.6

This is, because I had installed alternatives to python3.6.
When doing this the symlink '/usr/bin/python3' points to '/etc/alternatives/python3' which in turn points to '/usr/bin/python3.6'.

So the code of the function 'default_version' is (at least) incomplete.

Even I notice the problem as described above, the incorrect function 'default_version' is still presnt under Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS.

So I suggest that this merge was introduced into all active branches.
diff:
diff --git a/debian/py3versions.py b/debian/py3versions.py
index 76f9e6e..3936dd1 100755
--- a/debian/py3versions.py
+++ b/debian/py3versions.py
@@ -147,7 +147,7 @@ def supported_versions(version_only=False):
 def default_version(version_only=False):
     global _default_version
     if not _default_version:
-        _default_version = os.readlink('/usr/bin/python3')
+        _default_version = os.path.realpath('/usr/bin/python3', strict=False)
     # consistency check
     debian_default = read_default('default-version')
     if not _default_version in (debian_default, os.path.join('/usr/bin', debian_default)):
